title: modbusgen project
description: IWMAC Modbus list project file (replaces the Work sheet of the INAS Modbus Excel tool). One file per plant/table; the modbusgen tool validates it and generates the SQL import script. Field semantics: docs/02-inputs.md; authoring guide for AI agents: docs/11-ai-json-authoring.md. Cross-field rules the schema cannot express: every points[].group must be a key of groups (unless options.auto_groups fills it); every points[].statetext must be a key of statetexts; at least one point needs online: true; driver_id (function+addr+bit) and element_id must be unique across points.

$schema.description: Optional editor metadata - point it at this contract for inline validation; ignored by the tool. Use the published copy https://hapnes-dev.github.io/modbusgen-web/project.schema.json in files that travel, or ../schema/project.schema.json for files inside the repository. Convention: any field absent from the file is at its documented default.

_help.description: Free-form annotation for whoever opens the file next, human or agent - JSON's substitute for the comments YAML carries. Ignored by the tool: load_project strips it, and every JSON the tool writes replaces it with the current block (src/modbusgen/yamlio.py HELP_BLOCK), so editing it here changes nothing and is not preserved. Deliberately unconstrained in shape; the shipped form is an object of short prose lines covering what the file is, what generates from it, that an absent field is at its default, and the rules an agent cannot recover from the data (never invent a datatype/unit/scale key, one global subtract_one and no per-point subtraction, point order is the operator's view_order).

table.description: Table name <t> for iw_par_<t>_param / iw_par_<t>_groups / iw_set_<t>. Lowercase letters, digits, underscore. Ask the user - never invent it.

plant.description: Plant number, used only in the output file name. Prefer a string. Ask the user.

driver.description: Which IWMAC Modbus driver the plant runs (docs/15 section 1). Written into no SQL column - it decides what validation can conclude about word order and 32-bit writes, which the vendor document cannot settle. mb.exe supports word/byte swaps and FC16; modbus.php supports neither, so on it only _N datatypes read correctly and a writable 32-bit point cannot be written at all - both fail silently. mb.exe is the house standard and what a new project in the GUI starts with, so most files state it outright; modbus.php belongs in the file whenever the plant is known to run it. Absent or empty still means not stated - nobody said, not mb.exe - and leaves those checks as warnings that ask you to confirm.

options.description: Generation toggles, mirroring the Excel setup cells. Defaults are the template's shipped values - an authoring agent normally sets ONLY subtract_one and leaves the rest alone unless the user asks.

subtract_one.description: Subtract 1 from every Modbus address before building driver ids. true when the documentation numbers registers from 1 (most vendor docs, and all 4xxxx-style lists); false for zero-based protocol addresses. Never pre-subtract per point.

truncate.description: legacy sql_format only: emit TRUNCATE TABLE before the inserts. Ignored by modern, which uses REPLACE INTO.

create_tables.description: legacy sql_format only: emit CREATE TABLE. Ignored by modern, which always emits CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS.

use_system_no.description: Include each point's system_no in the alias text.

use_tag.description: Include each point's tag in the alias text.

use_extra.description: Append each point's extra in parentheses at the end of the alias.

reserve_text.description: Rows whose text equals this stay inactive (spare rows) even with force_active. Empty string disables the rule.

force_active.description: Every point gets active=1 regardless of its own active field (reserve_text rows still win).

include_minmax.description: Carry points[].range_min/range_max into the param record. Off leaves the columns blank, which is what the real fleet does.

use_json.description: Master gate on state texts (Excel Prot!B54): off = no format_extra JSON and no state list in the alias, regardless of per-point statetext ids.

statetext_only_rw.description: Emit state-text JSON only for writable (rw/vrw) points.

statetext_in_alias.description: Also flatten the state list into the point's extra, so it shows in the alias. Overwrites a hand-written extra on matched rows.

override_decimal.description: Fill the decimals column from the unit table's decimals entry, overwriting hand-typed values on matching units (Excel Prot!B46).

exclude_motherwords_from_groups.description: Keep motherword rows out of the groups block, so the operator menu shows the named bits rather than the raw word.

auto_motherwords.description: Synthesize the missing word row for bit-addressed points. Leave on; do not author motherword rows by hand.

auto_groups.description: Fill an empty points[].group from the datatype's default group.

alarms_to_alm.description: Move points with an alarm letter into the alm group. Only acts when auto_groups is also on.

proper_case_states.description: Proper-case state words (drift paa -> Drift Paa), matching Excel's WorksheetFunction.Proper.

encoding.description: Output file encoding. The IWMAC tables are latin1 - leave as cp1252.

require_motherwords.description: Promote a missing motherword from a soft warning to a hard validation error.

sql_format.description: modern = REPLACE INTO house style (2026 reference exports); legacy = the Excel tool's single-line INSERTs. Do not change without being asked.

system.description: Optional iw_sys_* blocks: physical device registration and driver communication settings. Omit the whole object unless the user asks for a complete/new-plant script - an existing plant already has these. Omitting it is fully supported; writing "system": null is neither required nor useful, and adding it does not affect GUI import. An imported or GUI-exported project carries "system": null because the source workbook enabled no iw_sys section - that is what the converter emits, not a serialisation style to copy when authoring. Nothing is emitted unless units and/or settings is true.

units.description: Emit one iw_sys_plant_units row per device (unit_list or the single-unit fields), plus the order-number link.

settings.description: Emit the iw_mb.exe process registration and all driver communication settings.

unit_id.description: Single-device form: device id in IWMAC.

unit_name.description: Single-device form: name the operator sees.

reg_type.description: Registration type recorded against the units. Usually blank.

order_no.description: Order number linked to the units in iw_sys_order_no.

owner.description: Driver/settings owner - it is the settings owner, the driver_type and the process name in one, e.g. EM270 or GRUNDFOS. IWMAC documents a maximum of 10 characters, capitals and digits only; both are reported by soft_checks as warnings rather than enforced, because the fleet contradicts them (docs/16).

driver_addr.description: Single-device form: Modbus slave address on the bus.

driver_addr_prefix.description: Prefix for device addresses: 0_ for the first driver on the plant, 1_ for the second.

view_order.description: Single-device form: sort position in the IWMAC device list.

unit_list.description: Several devices on one driver (Carel-style ID01..IDnn); overrides the single-unit fields.

driver_addr.description: Modbus slave address of this device.

comm.description: Driver communication settings (emitted with settings: true). tcp needs ip (+port); rtu needs com_port, baudrate, parity, stop_bits.

ip.description: tcp: IP of the device or gateway.

com_port.description: rtu: serial port on the IWMAC machine.

baudrate.description: rtu: the rate the bus is actually commissioned at, written verbatim into comm_baudrate. The Excel tool offered only 9600/19200 (a checkbox); the driver setting is a free numeric value, so the full standard ladder is allowed here - docs/10 divergence 15.

groups.description: Display grouping for the operator menu: group key -> display alias (or {alias, order}). Every group a point uses must exist here. Conventional default set: aio 'Analoge inn/ut', dio 'Digitale inn/ut', alm 'Alarmer', misc 'Diverse', sch 'Tidsskjema'. Keys are short lowercase mnemonics. An alias taken from a source document keeps that document's wording; the five above are the tool's own fallback for a document with no sections of its own.

oneOf.description: The display alias; order defaults to list position.

order.description: Explicit view order of the group itself. Two groups must not share one.

statetexts.description: Enumeration lists: list id -> {state number -> word}. Define each distinct vendor enumeration once and reference it from points via statetext: <id>. Keep the vendor's numbers exactly (>= 0 only - negative values cannot be state texts), and its words as printed - state words are not translated. Keys are digit strings in JSON.

datatypes.description: Datatype rows this project defines for itself - the Modbus_Variables!Z:AI table, carried in the file. Use only when no shipped key in data/tables/datatypes.csv fits; a name that already exists there must not be redefined. Every field should be a value the shipped table already uses, so the row is a new combination of primitives the IWMAC driver understands rather than a new primitive (docs/15).

read_func.description: Modbus read function: 1 coils, 2 discrete inputs, 3 holding registers, 4 input registers, 0 virtual. (Modbus_Variables!AA)

write_func.description: Modbus write function: 5 single coil, 6 single register, 16 multiple registers; empty for read-only. (AB)

raw_type.description: Raw type sent to the driver: X, I16, U16, I32, U32, F and the types added 2026-08-20 (D, CLK, STR4, BCD35, rU16 and the rest). (AC)

read_swap.description: Byte and word order on read: N normal, R reversed, W word-swapped. (AD)

write_swap.description: Byte and word order on write: N, R or W. (AE)

application.description: Digital IO | Analog values | Integral values | String values. (AF)

rw_hint.description: Informational read/write capability of the type. Excel does not read it and neither does modbusgen. (AH)

default_group.description: Group that auto_groups assigns to a point using this datatype and no group of its own: aio or dio. (AI)

points.description: One object per Modbus point, in the order the operator should see them (usually documentation order). This order decides the menu (view_order) - it is meaningful, not cosmetic.

group.description: Group key - must exist in groups. Required in practice; may be omitted only with options.auto_groups. (Work!A)

datatype.description: Key into data/tables/datatypes.csv, exactly as spelled there - never invented. Encodes presentation, register table, raw type and word order, e.g. A_Hold_I16_N, I_Hold_U16_N, Bit_Hold, Coil_X_N, A_Input_F_N. A name the shipped table does not carry is legal only when this project defines it in its own datatypes block (Custom_Hold_U32_W is the worked example of that, not a shipped key). (Work!D)

addr.description: Register/coil address exactly as the documentation prints it (strip 4xxxx/3xxxxx prefixes). Where a document prints both a Modicon-style register and an explicit protocol-address column, take the explicit one as printed and set subtract_one false - do not also strip a prefix or subtract again. options.subtract_one is the ONLY global offset conversion; never subtract per point. (Work!E)

bit.description: Bit number inside the register for Bit_* datatypes. 0-15 normally: the synthesized motherword is 16-bit and is never widened, because a 32-bit one would have to guess the word order. A bit of 16-31 is therefore a validation error UNLESS an explicit 32-bit point is authored at the same address, which commits to a word order and serves as the motherword. String form '5#4' = legacy nibble start#length. Do not author a motherword row otherwise - the tool synthesizes it. (Work!F)

element_id.description: Manual element_id override; rare - the tool derives <group>_<driver_id>. (Work!C)

system_no.description: Alias part 1: the plant system number, e.g. 360.001. Prefer a string - 360.010 as a number loses its trailing zero. Only when the user supplies a tag scheme. (Work!M)

tag.description: Alias part 2: short component tag, e.g. RT401. (Work!N)

text.description: Main alias text, the name the operator reads - short, and in the maker's own wording for the value: take it from the vendor document rather than translating it or inventing a description, so the list and the manual read side by side. The document's language is the list's language - a Norwegian manual gives Norwegian texts, an English one English; translating either way is the mistake. A bare register number is not a name; where the document supplies none, say so instead of shipping 'Register 4'. State words and group aliases follow the same rule - the document's words as printed. The only alias part always included; leaving it empty draws a validation warning. The literal 'Motherword' marks a motherword row - do not author those. (Work!P)

extra.description: Alias suffix in parentheses. Overwritten on generate when options.statetext_in_alias is on and the row has a statetext. (Work!O)

alarm.description: Alarm priority -> plant_pri. A = alarm (the fleet default for anything that is an alarm), N = note; B/C nearly unused. Omit for non-alarm points. (Work!R)

unit.description: Engineering unit, e.g. C for temperature, %, Pa, kWh: a key into data/tables/units.csv (case-insensitive), or a unit the table lacks written as the document prints it - that ships into eng_unit exactly as typed under a warning, 20 characters at most. Never a near-miss spelling of a key; omit when no unit is documented. (Work!S)

scale.description: Key into data/tables/scaling.csv matching the documented multiplier - x0.1 dominates real lists; INV inverts digitals. Omit for raw values. (Work!T)

rw.description: r read-only, rw writable - only when the documentation says so. vr/vrw are derived forms for bit rows; authoring agents write r or rw only. (Work!U)

update_freq.description: Polling override; omit for automatic (analog/integral: norm read-only / slow writable; digital: slow). Set slow on rarely-changing measured values like energy totals - they still log min/1.

online.description: Online-indication point - IWMAC uses these to see the unit is alive. Mark 3-4 reliable, always-readable points; validation fails with none. (Work!V)

active.description: Per-point active; ignored while options.force_active is on. (Work!W)

no_group.description: Keep this row out of the groups block (still a parameter, absent from the operator menu). (Work!X)

menu.description: Menu override; normally hand-patched after generation, not authored. (Work!AA)

decimals.description: Display decimals -> format %.Nf. Pair with the scale: x0.1 usually means 1. (Work!AB)

range_min.description: Engineering range minimum; only reaches the output with options.include_minmax. (Work!AC)

range_max.description: Engineering range maximum; only reaches the output with options.include_minmax. (Work!AD)

statetext.description: State-text list id - must exist as a key in statetexts. (Work!AE)
